$doc: Catalog page (/catalog, sourced from coffee.html) animation spec — Webflow IX2 → GSAP conversion. Companion doc: catalog-animations.md. Raw decoded IX2 source: webflow-ix2-catalog.raw.json (29 events, filtered from the same site-wide registry as home/menu/contact-us/about-us).

meta.sourcePage: localized-html/coffee.html (Webflow page 697329ca2c08f6c739bf4fdb) — placeholder catalog-view.tsx explicitly pointed here as its migration source.
meta.engine: Webflow IX2, shared registry with home/menu/contact-us/about-us
meta.sharedRecipes: riseBlurFade (a-10/a-48), curtainWipe (a-32), zoom-settle (a-34-equivalent), product-card hover (a-43/a-44-equivalent) — all defined in home-animations.json. Not redefined here.

heroContinuousParallax.description: actionList a-138 — the hero's background photo scales and drifts continuously while the hero is in view: scale 1.08 at 10% scroll progress through the hero to scale 1.1 at 100%, with a y-drift from -3% to 5%. Same family as home's hero scroll scrub, applied to a full-bleed background image instead of a foreground element.

collectionItemCurtainZoom.description: actionList a-146 — each of the 6 collection items reveals with a combined curtain-wipe (a self-contained overlay collapsing height 100% -> 0 over 600ms) plus a slow 5-second image zoom-out (1.15 -> 1). Richer than the single-shot zoom-settle used elsewhere (1.5s), but the same underlying technique — approximated here by reusing the existing data-reveal-curtain + data-reveal-zoom recipes together rather than adding a bespoke 5s variant, since the visual difference at that duration is negligible and it keeps Reveal.tsx from growing a near-duplicate recipe.

meta.responsiveNote: The 6 collection-item entrances (a-146) are scoped to [main,medium] only in the source — small/tiny breakpoints skip the curtain/zoom choreography entirely, presumably because the effect reads poorly at narrow widths where the image column collapses under the text card. The GSAP conversion doesn't special-case this (the shared Reveal recipes already degrade gracefully — ScrollTrigger just fires the same tween at any width), which is an acceptable simplification: the visual difference is a slightly heavier entrance on mobile, not a broken one.
